title: Powers of generators of the unit ideal generate the unit ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $s\subseteq R$ a subset generating the unit ideal, and $N\ge0$ an integer. Then $\{f^N: f\in s\}$ generates the unit ideal; that is, there are finitely many $f_1,\dots,f_n\in s$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n\in R$ with $\sum_ia_if_i^N=1$.

source.place: Lemma 00E0 (label lemma-Zariski-topology) (5), (8), (16): a prime contains $f^N$ iff it contains $f$, so $V(\{f^N\})=V(s)=V((s))=\emptyset$, hence $(\{f^N\})=R$ ($N\ge1$; for $N=0$ the set is $\{1\}$ or $s=\emptyset$, $R=0$)

mathlib_searches.query: if s generates the unit ideal then the n-th powers of elements of s generate the unit ideal
